title_working: The Day the Dot-com Boom Peaked

paragraphs.text: On March 10, 2000, the Nasdaq Composite peaked at 5,048.62. At that moment, the index was worth more than double what it had been a year earlier.

spec.small: Nasdaq Composite, all-time high of the era

paragraphs.text: Then it broke. By October 2002, the Nasdaq had fallen to 1,114.11, a loss of 78% from its peak.
Pets.com, founded in 1998, became famous for its sock-puppet mascot. On November 9, 2000, it went out of business, only nine months after its IPO.
The motto of the era was get big fast. The full story is on the channel.
